canonical.behaviour: Makes workflow-axa faster without making it less correct, as agreed in agreement 1 (items 1-16). Hooks: a call that writes nothing skips the transcript parse, the parse reads only new lines, the after-call hook no longer runs on Read, and old-task code loads only when an old task exists. Reading: the router reads its SKILL.md, the recipe index and one recipe; rare sections move to files read only when needed; each repeated rule lives in one file. Stops: one-ticket work gets no separate agreement question, grilling asks in one round, and the lightweight offer has two answers (Approve, Change something). Review: one reviewer for a small diff, findings must reproduce, docs_check runs less often. Execution: recipe steps go into the todo list and each ticket gets a fresh context. Every change still gets an offer and the hook still refuses writes outside it. Work runs as tickets T0-T8 in this worktree, with parallel subagents on separate files, a measure and test loop, and live pilots within 50 USD in total.
exclusions: VALIDATION.md and other commands AGENTS.md says need the owner's OK each time
anything in D:/workflow-axa (the live checkout), global settings and installed copies
pushing, merging into main, releasing, version bumps and reinstalling
conditions: Commits only on speed/2.10 after a green round
Live pilots run in a throwaway fixture under .artifacts/2026-11-19-workflow-speed/, at most 5 USD per run and 50 USD in total
No test is removed or weakened; a moved sentence keeps its test
Parallel workers never share a file
checks: a live bug-fix pilot on the candidate gets the same result as on main, in less time and with fewer tokens
hook allow and refuse results are unchanged on the recorded cases
the full unittest suite passes, with failures that existed before named
tools/measure_speed.py shows at most 10k words before code for a one-ticket bug fix and read-only hook time that does not grow with session length
